Expanding gives exactly 18 linear vectors; max over a unit sphere equals the largest vector norm. Algebraically comparing three dominating squared norms produces the sharp sqrt(7/5) aspect boundary, two conditional height switches, and the unique 2+4+8=14 multicritical equality. With an explicit gap q below M, every nonwinning cap vanishes and winning equal-radius caps are disjoint: this proves the exact linear upper tail and exponential maximum-sampling limit, for every permitted parameter and every threshold in [q,M]. The independently implemented projected-vertex convex-hull checker passed 14,400 area comparisons across 12 shape regimes, plus all exact winners, transition counts and finite cap-separation inequalities. It is corroboration, not a substitute for the proof.
